The proposal is in the format required by the Board of Governors for Higher Education. A.GENERAL INFORMATION 1. Name of institution University of Rhode Island 2. Names of administrative units Kinesiology Department College of Human Science and Services 3. Title of proposed organizational unit Physical Therapy Department 4. Intended date of change Upon Board of Governors approval 5. Intended location of organizational unit University of Rhode Island, Kingston Campus

Summary description of the proposed organization change. The purpose of this proposal is to change the standing of the Physical Therapy Program from a program within the Kinesiology Department to a separate Department within the College of Human Science and Services. 8. Signature of the President ______________________________ Robert L. Carothers 9. Resources The organizational changes proposed herein require no new resources. The Physical Therapy Program has its own director, faculty, secretarial support, facilities, and operating budget. 10. Person to be contacted during the review Diane Horm Associate Dean College of Human Science and Services diane@uri.edu 874-2403 Beth Marcoux, PT, PhD Program Director Physical Therapy bmarcoux@mail.uri.edu 874-5627 11. Signed agreements for cooperative arrangements. None

3 B.RATIONALE This organizational change is being proposed because the Physical Therapy Program can better fulfill its mission to educate competent doctors of physical therapy who can provide skilled patient care in a variety of settings, conduct clinical research, and provide service to the community at large if it is an academic department within the College of Human Science and Services rather than a program within the Kinesiology Department.
The mission of the Physical Therapy Program focuses on professional, graduate rather than undergraduate education as is the case in the Kinesiology Department.
There are no common students between the two units nor does faculty teach across the units.
The reorganization will allow PT faculty to focus their efforts on continued development and advancement of the program, clinical and basic science research related to the profession and provision of service to the community and profession.
The Physical Therapy Program has functioned autonomously within the (Department of Physical Education now renamed) Kinesiology Department since its inception in 1991.

It has had its own faculty, support staff, facilities, and budget from the very beginning as a requirement of professional accreditation.
Further, due to accreditation requirements, the Program Director has maintained direct communication with the Dean of the College and was a regular participant at College Management meetings.
A self-study report for the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education was recently completed in preparation for a site visit that occurred in September 2005.
It was during this self- evaluation that the faculty recognized that the Program was intended to be a separate entity within the college from its development and that separation would allow for better overall functioning of the program.
With the recent move from the masters of physical therapy to the doctor of physical therapy, the program is even more out of place being located within the Kinesiology Department.
Separation will allow better collaboration between the Physical Therapy Program and other departments such as Communicative Disorders and Biology.

This re- organization will simplify day-to-day operations and clarify evaluation of program activities because data will no longer be combined with that of the Kinesiology department.
Please note that no new resources are needed to affect this organizational change.

RATIONALE The College of Pharmacy presently consists of three Departments: The Department of Applied Pharmaceutical Science (APS); The Department of Biomedical Science (BMS) and the Department of Pharmacy Practice (PHP).
Faculty in PHP are primarily clinicians, who are directly involved in patient care and as a result are primarily based at clinical sites throughout the state.
In contrast, faculty in APS and BMS are based at the Kingston campus.

As pharmaceutical science and biomedical science has evolved in the last decade there has been an increasing overlap in the research activities of the two departments.
However, the present departmental structure discourages collaboration and hinders interaction between and among faculty.

The proposed departmental structure would address this problem and hopefully lead to cross-fertilization of research efforts between the two existing departments.
Owing to the more practice oriented research activities of the PE/PE section of APS, a more logical placement for this section would be within the department of PHP.
These organizational changes will also enable the College to address its graduate program and consider ways to make the program more cost-effective and to better prepare the graduates for careers in pharmaceutical and biological science.

Assessment of Student Learning Outcomes
8.59.10 Assessment of student learning outcomes shall be coordinated by the Assistant Director of Student Learning, Outcomes Assessment and Accreditation (see 2.22.21 ) with the oversight of the JAPROA (see Sections 5.84.10 – 5.84.14). The following policies shall apply to this process: #23-24-7
8.59.11 Academic Program Engagement: All undergraduate, professional, and graduate academic programs, including General Education, shall be actively engaged in student learning outcomes assessment as evidenced by, but not limited to:
a) Published student learning outcomes that are clear statements of what students are expected to gain, achieve, demonstrate, or know at the completion of the academic program. These student learning outcomes shall be published on the program’s website as well as on the website for the Office of Student Learning, Outcomes Assessment, and Accreditation (SLOAA). These student learning outcomes shall be periodically reviewed by the academic program for ongoing relevance.

b) A plan of student learning outcomes assessment that is endorsed by the program’s faculty. Plans should include a regular and predictable cycle for collecting and analyzing assessment data, for discussing curricular and programmatic changes, for implementing interventions, and for re-assessing the impact of implemented changes. Outcomes assessment plans will be published on each program’s website as well as on the SLOAA website.
c) Reports of student learning outcomes assessment that are provided to SLOAA using staggered cycles of no more than 3 years. Cycles for accredited programs will be adjusted to decrease redundancy of effort. #09-10–29

8.59.12 SLOAA Guidance for Academic Programs: Guidelines and schedules for preparation of outcomes assessment plans and reports shall be provided by SLOAA with the assistance and approval of the Joint Committee on Academic Program Review and Outcomes Assessment (JAPROA). SLOAA shall offer advice on the logistics of collecting assessment data, support for analyzing the results, and feedback on designing curricular and programmatic changes. Rubrics for evaluating the plans and reports shall be generated by SLOAA and posted on its website. #09-10–29 #23-24-7
8.59.13 Evaluation of Plans and Reports: Student learning outcomes assessment plans and reports shall be submitted through SLOAA for evaluation and recommendations by JAPROA. Programs shall be notified directly of the results of the evaluation and whether modification is needed. Summary reports shall be published on the SLOAA website. JAPROA shall provide a general summary of outcomes assessment in its annual report. #09-10–29 #23-24-7
